summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and functional quadriplegia was admitted with fever, tachypnea, tachycardia, and hypotension. He was found to have a complicated urinary tract infection caused by Providencia rettgeri and hospital-associated pneumonia with pulmonary edema. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics initially, then narrowed to cefepime based on culture results. His sepsis resolved, hypotension improved with fluids and brief pressor support, and hypernatremia corrected with free water. Renal function returned to baseline. He was discharged to extended care on day 5 to complete a 10-day course of IV cefepime, with follow-up planned for pulmonary and infectious disease.
problems: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with (acute) lower respiratory infection
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Paralysis of vocal cords and larynx, unspecified
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
